APC.hq_address: 40 Blantyre Street, off Adetokunbo Ademola Crescent, Wuse II, Abuja, FCT
APC.description: The All Progressives Congress is one of Nigeria's two major political parties, formed in February 2013 through a merger of opposition parties. It won the presidency in 2015 with Muhammadu Buhari and remains the ruling party under President Bola Tinubu.

PDP.hq_address: Wadata Plaza, Michael Okpara Way, Wuse Zone 5, Abuja
PDP.description: The Peoples Democratic Party is one of Nigeria's two major political parties, founded in 1998. It governed at the federal level from 1999 to 2015 and is now the main opposition party; its national leadership has been the subject of factional disputes in 2025-2026.

LP.hq_address: No. 2 IBM Haruna Street, Utako, Abuja, FCT
LP.description: The Labour Party (Nigeria) is a centre-left, social-democratic party founded in 2002 (originally the Party for Social Democracy). It rose to national prominence in 2022 when Peter Obi joined and became its 2023 presidential candidate.
LP._notes: Party has publicly disowned the @LabourPartyNG handle; no official social handles recorded. Nenadi Usman elected/court-affirmed national chairman (Apr 2026); Julius Abure faction still contests.

NNPP.hq_address: No 11, Mahatma Gandhi Street, Area 11, Garki, Abuja, FCT
NNPP.description: The New Nigeria Peoples Party is a populist Nigerian party founded in 2002 by Boniface Aniebonam, predominantly active in Kano State. It gained national prominence in 2022 when Rabiu Kwankwaso joined and ran as its 2023 presidential candidate.
NNPP._notes: leader_name (national chairman) omitted: chairmanship contested/unresolved in 2026 (Ajuji Ahmed / Agbo Major / Bala Yunusa Mohammed variously cited).

APGA.hq_address: Plot 1160 Cadastral Zone B07, Katampe District, FCT Abuja
APGA.description: The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) is a Nigerian political party registered in 2002, historically the dominant party in Anambra State and currently led at state level by Governor Chukwuma Soludo. It espouses nationalism, federalism and progressivism.
APGA.slogan: To be your brother's and sister's keeper

ADC.hq_address: 2 Adetokunbo Ademola Crescent, Wuse, Abuja 900288, FCT
ADC.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) is a Nigerian political party founded in 2005 that in 2025 became the adopted platform of a broad opposition coalition aiming to challenge the ruling APC ahead of the 2027 elections. Former Senate President David Mark serves as its interim national chairman.

SDP.hq_address: No 17 Nairobi Street, Wuse II, Abuja
SDP.description: The Social Democratic Party (SDP) is a centre-left Nigerian political party. Tracing its name and heritage to the original SDP created in 1989 (whose candidate M.K.O. Abiola won the 1993 election), the current party was re-registered with INEC in December 2002 and has re-emerged as a notable opposition platform.
SDP._notes: logo_url not reliably sourced; left null.

YPP.hq_address: Block 10, Flat No. 1, Benue Crescent, Area 1, Garki, Abuja
YPP.description: The Young Progressives Party (YPP) is a Nigerian social-democratic and progressive party registered by INEC on 7 June 2017, formed to offer a youth-oriented alternative to the dominant APC and PDP.
YPP._notes: color left null: logo is tri-color (yellow/red/green), no single sourced dominant hex.

AA.description: Action Alliance is a Nigerian political party registered by INEC in 2005. In recent years it has been marked by a protracted national leadership dispute between factions led by Kenneth Udeze and Adekunle Omoaje, with conflicting court rulings and INEC recognitions.
AA._notes: leader_name (Kenneth Udeze) is contested: a Court of Appeal affirmed Udeze (Nov 2025) while INEC at one point recognised Adekunle Omoaje (Dec 2025). Lower-confidence.

AAC.hq_address: Office 011, Bolingo Hotel & Towers, Plot 777 Independence Avenue, Central Business District, Abuja
AAC.description: The African Action Congress (AAC) is a left-wing Nigerian political party founded on 15 August 2018 by activist and Sahara Reporters publisher Omoyele Sowore. It is closely associated with the 'Take It Back' movement and espouses anti-establishment, pro-people politics.

Accord.description: Accord (also known as the Accord Party) is a Nigerian political party registered by INEC, headquartered in Abuja. It is a centre-right party with strongholds historically in Oyo State.
Accord._notes: founding_year not reliably sourced (Wikipedia infobox blank); left null.

ADP.hq_address: Plot 3379A/3379B, Mungo Park Close, Off Jesse Jackson/Gimbya Street, Asokoro/Garki Area 11, Abuja
ADP.description: The Action Democratic Party (ADP) is a Nigerian political party founded in June 2017 and registered by INEC in December 2017, positioning itself as a 'third force' alternative to the APC and PDP. Its national chairman is Engr. Yabagi Sani.

APP.hq_address: Plot 1077, Cadastral Zone B2, Area 3 Junction, Durumi, Abuja
APP.description: Action Peoples Party (APP) is an INEC-registered Nigerian political party headquartered in Durumi, Abuja, whose acronym is APP. Its most prominent figure is Hon. Ikenga Ugochinyere (National Leader), with Barr. Uchenna Nnadi as National Chairman. It has won local-government seats in Rivers and Jigawa states and is positioning for the 2027 general elections.
APP._notes: NAME DISCREPANCY — IDENTITY NOW CONFIRMED, NAME NOT AUTO-CHANGED. INEC's acronym 'APP' maps to 'Action Peoples Party' (self-styled 'Action People's Party'); the DB row's name 'All Progressives Party' does NOT correspond to any INEC-registered party and is incorrect. Per task §1 ('name is never touched'), the seed scripts do NOT change the name — it requires a human decision. Recommended correction (sourced via inecnigeria.org + actionpeoplesparty.com): UPDATE political_parties SET name='Action Peoples Party' WHERE acronym='APP' AND name='All Progressives Party'. Profile fields and officers (Nnadi/Bossan/Ugochinyere) were populated for this confirmed party. Also note: a Federal High Court ordered APP's deregistration ~16 Jun 2026 (with ADC, AA, Accord, ZLP), stayed by the Court of Appeal 17 Jun 2026 — APP remains registered pending appeal.

PRP.description: The Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) is a left-wing Nigerian party founded on 27 September 1978 by Marxist intellectuals and supporters of Mallam Aminu Kano, rooted in his radical/talakawa (commoner) socialist tradition. It is one of the longest-surviving party brands in Nigeria's history.
PRP._notes: Hakeem Baba-Ahmed elected chairman at 28 Mar 2026 convention and INEC-recognised; a faction has petitioned INEC disputing it.

ZLP.hq_address: Dabo Shopping Mall, Suite 206, 2nd Floor, 73 Ladoke Boulevard, Garki, Abuja
ZLP.description: The Zenith Labour Party (ZLP) is an INEC-registered Nigerian party that rose to prominence in 2018 when former Ondo State governor Olusegun Mimiko adopted it as his presidential platform. It is led by Dan Nwanyanwu, a former national chairman of the Labour Party.
ZLP._notes: founding_year 2018 inferred (Wikipedia lists 'Unknown'); ZLP color is tri-color, red chosen as dominant.

APM.name: Allied Peoples Movement
APM.hq_address: Plot 232, No. 2 Leventis Building, Samuel Adesujo Ademulegun Street, Off Muhammadu Buhari Way, Central Business District, Abuja FCT
APM.description: Allied Peoples Movement (APM) is an INEC-registered Nigerian political party registered in August 2018. The party operates on principles of good governance, national development, and citizens' empowerment, with a motto of 'Integrity, Sacrifice, Service.' APM._notes: Officers/address/phone from INEC party page (authoritative). twitter/facebook not reliably sourced; left null. founding_year = INEC registration year (Aug 2018).

BP.name: Boot Party
BP.hq_address: House 11 Road C1, F.H.A Karu, Abuja
BP.description: Boot Party (BP), whose acronym stands for "Because Of Our Tomorrow," is a Nigerian political party registered by INEC on 25 September 2019. It describes itself as a cooperative-style, technology-and-people-driven movement committed to anti-corruption, youth empowerment, and national restructuring through dialogue. Its political platform, branded "One Working Nigeria (OWN)," promotes universal healthcare, housing, renewable energy, and job creation.
BP._notes: Officers/address/phone from INEC page. color not reliably sourced; left null. founding_year = INEC registration (25 Sep 2019).

DLA.name: Democratic Leadership Alliance
DLA.hq_address: No.25 Niger Street, Sun City Estate, Galadimawa, Abuja.

DLA.slogan: Leading with Courage, Serving with Integrity

NDP.name: National Democratic Party
NDP.hq_address: No. 3 Ontario Crescent, SunCity Estate, Galadimawa, Abuja
NDP.description: The National Democratic Party (NDP) is a Nigerian political party founded on 5 June 2024 by Hon. Ada Elizabeth Fredrick Okwori. NDP.slogan: Light of hope, Nigeria first, Bright future for all

NRM.name: National Rescue Movement

NRM._notes: Officers/address/phone from INEC page. founding_year = INEC registration (Dec 2017).

YP.name: Youth Party

YP.ideology: Youth empowerment; good governance; service-oriented leadership; anti-corruption; social equity
YP._notes: Officers/address/phone/party-email from INEC page. founding_year = INEC registration (16 Aug 2018; organising began 2015–2016). color not sourced; left null.
